features: THE SHARES THAT ADDED UP TO TWO HUNDRED — No migration: the database is not touched. What changes is what the import writes: from this version, in one precise case, it writes less than before and says so. Re-importing a corrected file is the normal gesture of a migration — you see that the spouses came in as a single subject, you split the couple in the file, you re-import expecting the correction to take the place of the old data. Instead the two versions of the data lived side by side, and on the unit the shares added up to 200 %.

WHY THE GUARD THAT WAS THERE COULD NOT BE ENOUGH. The idempotency check existed and worked: it compared the triple unit, person, role and refused to rewrite the same row. But on the second import the person is different — the couple as a single subject and the two spouses on their own are three distinct records — so no triple collided, every row went in, and no point of the importer looked at the shares already present on the unit. Established on the test database: a building that had received three imports had two units out of eleven at 200 %.

WHAT IT DOES NOW. When the file and the archive disagree on who is linked to a unit, the import skips that unit and writes it in the report, with the name of the unit and the role in question — owner or tenant, because the file carries tenants too, and sending you to look at the owners for a conflict about a lease is sending you to look at the wrong thing. Nothing changes in the archive, and the conflict appears among the things «to check», with the button that leads to the units.

AND WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT DO. It does not delete, it does not replace and it does not ask anything. The path that asked «replace or skip» had been written and then withdrawn by the review: the question was not reachable from any screen, and the import stayed stuck forever with half the work already written. Whoever needs to correct an ownership does it on the unit's own page, where the shares are visible while they change.

A CLOSED DOOR THAT WOULD NOT REOPEN. This version's review found a nearby, silent defect: if a unit had a terminated ownership with the same triple, the check counted it as existing and the file's row did not go in. No warning said so. The unit was left with no active holder — which is exactly the state in which it receives no instalments, appears in no arrears and enters no allocation. The three reads that look at ownership now agree on the same filter.

THE REST. The page «To check after the import» had no navigation trail at the top: now it does, with the same two entries as the neighbouring pages of the management area. Outside the program, this version brings an internal command that measures the state of the documentation — age, references that no longer resolve, work items the index does not list — and archives concluded documents instead of leaving them among the living ones.
